subject: general
question: 8 years ago, the age of a father was 21 years more than twice his son's age. After how many years, from now, will he be twice his son's age?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **son's age** 8 years ago be x. Then **father's age** was 2x + 21.

Age difference between them = (2x + 21) − x = **x + 21**.

Age difference remains **constant** always.

When father becomes **twice** his son's age, let son's age be S. Then Father = 2S.

Difference = 2S − S = S. Therefore, S = x + 21.

Son's age 8 years ago was x; now it is x + 8. Future age S = x + 21 is (x + 21) − (x + 8) = **13 years** from now.

**∴ The correct answer is 13 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 8 years ago, Father = 2 × Son + 21.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/641197892e4cb8854c428da0694e9300c182bbd39c422d3a53d35ab9560e0698.png] 

Let the present age of **Father** be F and **Son** be S.

⇒ (F − 8) = 2(S − 8) + 21

⇒ F − 8 = 2S − 16 + 21

⇒ F − 2S = 13 ... (i)

Let the required time from now be **t years**.

⇒ (F + t) = 2(S + t)

⇒ F + t = 2S + 2t

⇒ F − 2S = t ... (ii)

Comparing equation (i) and (ii):

⇒ t = 13 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 13 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Constant Age Difference

The difference between the ages of two people always remains the same, regardless of how many years pass.

Ratio Method for Ages

If the ratio of ages changes from a:b to c:d over x years, ensure the numerical difference between ratio parts (a-b) and (c-d) is equal by multiplying appropriately.

Equation Balancing

When a statement says 'A is n years more than m times B', the equation is A = mB + n.</p
